source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 19 — SPIRITS OF FALLEN WATCHERS + WOMEN-AS-SIRENS — Aramaic preserved partial in 4Q205 1 xi; Greek Akhmim 19:1-3 substantially complete; Ge'ez full. Uriel as angelic guide. The 'women-as-sirens' (γυναῖκες σειρῆνες) gloss is one of the most distinctive lexical sites.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶπέν μοι Οὐριήλ· Ἐνταῦθα στήσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι οἱ συμμίξαντες ταῖς γυναιξίν, καὶ τὰ πνεύματα αὐτῶν πολυμόρφοι γενόμενοι λυμαίνονται τοὺς ἀνθρώπους καὶ πλανήσουσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ θύειν τοῖς δαιμονίοις ὡς θεοῖς, ἕως ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης κρίσεως, ἐν ᾗ κριθήσονται εἰς ἀποτελείωσιν.
verses.translit: Kai eipen moi Ouriēl; Entautha stēsontai hoi angeloi hoi symmixantes tais gynaixin, kai ta pneumata autōn polymorphoi genomenoi lymainontai tous anthrōpous kai planēsousin autous eis to thyein tois daimoniois hōs theois, heōs hēmeras tēs megalēs kriseōs, en hē krithēsontai eis apoteleiōsin.
verses.text_geez: ወይቤለኒ፡ ዑርኤል፡ ዝየ፡ ይቀውሙ፡ መላእክት፡ እለ፡ ተደመሩ፡ ምስለ፡ አንስት፡ ወመናፍስቲሆሙ፡ ብዙኃነ፡ ራእይ፡ እንዘ፡ ይከውኑ፡ ያኀሥሙ፡ ለሰብእ፡ ወያስሕትዎሙ፡ ከመ፡ ይሥውዑ፡ ለአጋንንት፡ ከመ፡ ለአማልክት፡ እስከ፡ ዕለተ፡ ኵነኔ፡ ዐባይ፡ በዘይትኴነኑ፡ ለፍጻሜ፡
verses.witness_secondary: 4Q205 1 xi partial (Milik 1976 pp. 220-223) — Aramaic of Uriel-speech partly preserved
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS SITE — DAEMONOLOGICAL ETIOLOGY.** Uriel reveals: the angels who mingled with women are the source of the demonic spirits who lead humans astray to sacrifice to demons as gods. **This is the foundational text for the etiology of pagan idolatry-as-demonic-deception in Second Temple Judaism + early Christianity**: cf. Deut 32:17, Ps 106:37, 1 Cor 10:20 ('what pagans sacrifice they sacrifice to demons'), Rev 9:20. The 'spirits of the giants' as demons is the central daemonological doctrine of 1 En 15-16, here re-stated.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τῶν παραβάντων ἀγγέλων εἰς σειρῆνας γενήσονται.
verses.translit: Kai hai gynaikes tōn parabantōn angelōn eis seirēnas genēsontai.
verses.witness_primary: Akhmim Panopolitanus 19:2 (Black 1985 p. 52) — KEY Greek lexeme σειρῆνες
verses.notes: **WOMEN-AS-SIRENS (σειρῆνες / sereyn).** One of the most distinctive lexical features of the Akhmim Greek 1 Enoch. The Greek translator (or the underlying Aramaic tradition) renders the wives of the Watchers as becoming 'sirens' — likely deriving from Hebrew/Aramaic for night-creatures or wailing spirits. **Cross-corpus**: cf. Isa 13:21-22, 34:14, Jer 50:39 (LXX renders Hebrew demons-of-the-wilderness as sirēnes in some passages); cf. Homer Od. 12 (the Sirens as seductive death-singers). The translator chose a Greco-Roman mythological category to render a Semitic demonological one — a rare site of explicit cross-cultural lexicalization in 1 Enoch.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἐγὼ Ἑνὼχ μόνος εἶδον τὴν θεωρίαν, τὰ πέρατα πάντων, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδῃ ἄνθρωπος ὡς ἐγὼ εἶδον.
verses.translit: Kai egō Henōch monos eidon tēn theōrian, ta perata pantōn, kai ou mē idē anthrōpos hōs egō eidon.
verses.text_geez: ወአንሰ፡ ሄኖክ፡ ባሕቲትየ፡ ርእኩ፡ ራእየ፡ አጽናፈ፡ ኵሉ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ብእሲ፡ ዘይሬኢ፡ ከመ፡ ዘርእኩ፡ አንሰ፡
verses.notes: Enoch's first-person closing testimony — 'I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things, and no man shall see as I have seen.' Inexpressibility-topos + privileged-seer-formula. cf. 2 Cor 12:1-4. Closes the first cosmic-tour cycle (chs 17-19).
